findings.summary: People are destroyed when every primary (founder) department is empty: coming-of-age shares are apportioned over primary departments only, and apportion returns zeros when their total is 0, while children are still removed. Conservation (total = start + births - deaths) breaks.
findings.evidence: Two-department test pack: total - (200+births-deaths) = 0 at year 86, -2 at 87, -4 at 88 (founders [1,..,1,..] -> [0,..,0,..]; children 37 constant). Also shares weight founders only, ignoring ship-born, so department sizes drift toward equal once founders thin out. Founders pack at year 100 (hold, no events): delta 0 only because 1 founder survives in most departments at the 90+ mortality of 15 percent a year; they die out by about year 130. Latent beyond the century; no test covers it.

findings.summary: The batched == daily claim holds only without events or year boundaries in the skip. Years are all run before drift, and events are heard before the weekly decays, so a multi-year or event-containing advance differs from day-by-day.
findings.evidence: My tests: daily vs batched over 3 years (yearsTo then drift) returned false; daily (event at day 20) vs batched (event heard first, advance to 30) returned false. CHANGELOG/outcome say batched and daily agree; the code comment only concedes signals/shortages at 7 and 365 boundaries. The repo test covers 9 ticks (no week boundary beyond 7, event at 10 outside) and a 60-tick drift with no events or years, so it cannot catch this. Signals and shortNow are sampled once at the end state of an advance, not per week/year.

findings.summary: The promoted record does not match the naming contract written in the sprint plan: contract is {kind:promoted,id:<cohort>-p<n>,cohort,at}; implementation emits role, person, cohort, reason, at with no id key.
findings.evidence: trace string builds kv(kind, role, person, cohort, reason, at); plan 'Naming contract' says id. The integration agent keying on id will not find it.

Sprint JSON status is still in_progress with P7 passes null.
findings.evidence: Claim runs in CHANGELOG say 'seeds 1..3'; no cap test in cohorts_test/population_test; split-escalates claim passes by pack construction (archive set half content/half breaking), so it checks plumbing, not emergence.

findings.summary: Century figure and calibration: 1,646 vs the claim limit 1,650 is a 4-person margin, and rates were retuned (60/30/8 to 70/48/20) after the ship died out, which is disclosed. My own no-event, no-shortage run of the founders pack gives about 1,541 at year 100 (the cohorts.ail comment says about 1,540), so the 1,646 depends on sim conditions; CHANGELOG and code comment disagree without explanation.
findings.evidence: e4 run: sum of cohort headcounts at year 100 = 1,541.

findings.summary: A user group id ending in -shipborn is treated as non-primary; id validation allows it. Also ${id}-shipborn can exceed the 48-character id limit.
findings.evidence: goodId permits it; endsWith9 only checks the suffix.
